title: Thousands March in Mexico City in Support of Cuba, 73 Years After the Assault on the Moncada Barracks, Against US Attacks on the Island
author: Jared Laureles and Iván Evair Saldaña
content:
_This article by Jared Laureles and Iván Evair Saldaña originally appeared in
the[July 26, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/07/26/politica/colectivos-y-
cubanos-en-cdmx-se-alistan-para-marchar-hoy-a-73-anos-del-asalto-al-cuartel-
moncada), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City.** In a context marked by the escalation of United States
attacks against Cuba, dozens of people are holding a march for the 73rd
anniversary of the assault on the Moncada Barracks, considered the start of
the Revolution led by Fidel Castro against the dictatorship of Fulgencio
Batista.

**The mobilization, which began shortly after 11:00 a.m. heading toward the
former US embassy, will also be carried out as an act of solidarity with the
island and in rejection of the recent threats of aggression and invasion made
by President Donald Trump, emphasized Francisco Rosas, coordinator of the
Colectivo Solidaridad Militante Va Por Cuba.**

![Marchers carry Cuban flags and a red-and-black July 26 Movement banner
reading '26 Julio'](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/2026-07-26-cuba-moncada-march-03-flags.jpg)Photo: Luis
Castillo

"Solidarity mobilization of all sister peoples becomes urgent, because Cuban
sovereignty must be defended, but in that process also the sovereignty of all
countries and the right to free self-determination," stated Jaime García, a
member of this collective.

Olivia Garza, vice president of the Association of Cubans Residing in Mexico
"José Martí," affirmed that this July 26 they are taking to the streets in the
unitary march to stress that the real threat is the blockade imposed by the
United States more than six decades ago.

> "Cuba is not alone. Cuba is not a threat; the blockade is. The solidarity of
> the Mexican people is present in this battle that we must make great in the
> face of imperialist aggression," she expressed.

![A demonstrator holds a placard depicting Donald Trump with a Pinocchio nose
beside a Cuban flag](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/2026-07-26-cuba-moncada-march-05-trump-
placard.jpg)Photo: Luis Castillo

> **" No to the war against Cuba. Down with the blockade! To defend Cuba is to
> defend Mexico," reads a banner leading the mobilization.**

![Marchers hold a banner reading 'No to the war against Cuba! Down with the
blockade! To defend Cuba is to defend
Mexico!'](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/2026-07-26-cuba-moncada-march-02-banner.jpg)Photo:
Luis Castillo

At the Hemiciclo, members of the Association of Cubans Residing in Mexico,
along with peasant and solidarity organizations, gathered, expressing with
Cuban flags their support for the island's sovereignty.** "Cuba yes, Yankees
no!" are some of the chants they shout.**

In front of the Hemiciclo, a "Tlalmanali" altar was set up, where attendees
perform a ritual greeting to the directions of the native peoples.

![An effigy caricaturing US Secretary of State Marco Rubio holding a Trump
puppet is carried through the march](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/2026-07-26-cuba-moncada-march-04-rubio-
effigy.jpg)Photo: Luis Castillo

The walk has as its destination the former United States Embassy in Mexico, on
Paseo de la Reforma, where, in a statement backed by a hundred civil
organizations and collectives, they will express their rejection of the
economic, commercial, and financial blockade imposed on the island.
